title: Configuration & Settings
summary: Manage settings with pydantic-settings, .env files, and dependency injection.

sections.content: Use pydantic-settings to load configuration from environment variables and .env files. One Settings object, used everywhere.

sections.title: .env must be in .gitignore
sections.content: Never commit .env files. In production, inject env vars via Docker/Kubernetes instead of a file.
@lru_cache on get_settings() avoids re-parsing .env per request — the Settings object is created once and cached.
pydantic-settings automatically coerces string env vars to the correct types:

import pytest
from config import get_settings

def test_debug_off():
    settings = Settings(DATABASE_URL="sqlite://", SECRET_KEY="test", DEBUG=False)
    assert settings.DEBUG is False

def test_custom_settings():
    # Override for tests
    test_settings = Settings(DATABASE_URL="sqlite://", SECRET_KEY="test")
    assert test_settings.DATABASE_URL == "sqlite://"

code_challenge.title: Settings with Dependency Injection
code_challenge.description: Create a FastAPI app with a Settings class (DATABASE_URL, DEBUG) loaded from environment. Add GET /config that returns {"debug": settings.DEBUG}.
hints: Create an annotated type: SettingsDep = Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)]
code_challenge.note: The default DEBUG is False — TestClient sees this default since no env vars are set

quiz.question: Why use pydantic-settings instead of os.getenv()?
options: Type validation, .env support, defaults, and dependency injection
quiz.explanation: pydantic-settings provides type coercion (string → int/bool), .env file loading, defaults, validation, and seamless dependency injection.

quiz.question: What does @lru_cache on get_settings() do?
options: Creates Settings once and caches the object (avoids re-parsing .env)
quiz.explanation: @lru_cache ensures get_settings() is called once — the Settings object is created once and reused. This avoids re-reading and parsing the .env file on every request.

quiz.question: How does pydantic-settings handle DEBUG=false in .env?
options: It coerces to bool False automatically
quiz.explanation: pydantic-settings coerces the string 'false' to bool False automatically. Same for integers ('60' → 60) and lists.

quiz.question: Where should .env files be tracked?
quiz.explanation: .env files contain secrets and must NEVER be committed. Add .env to .gitignore. In production, inject env vars via Docker/Kubernetes.

quiz.question: How do you use settings in a route?
quiz.explanation: Use dependency injection: settings: SettingsDep = Annotated[Settings, Depends(get_settings)]. This allows overriding settings in tests via dependency_overrides.
